condition: suspected acute pulmonary embolism after long-haul flight presenting with hemoptysis
level_rationale: New-onset coughing up blood today in a 31-year-old woman on oral contraceptives the day after a 12-hour flight indicates suspected acute pulmonary embolism requiring immediate emergency hospital evaluation, whereas coughing up yellow phlegm today without hemoptysis, dyspnea, or chest pain points to an uncomplicated respiratory infection warranting non-emergent outpatient clinic evaluation.

everyday_sources.evidence: Chest pain, especially while breathing in, coughing up blood, and shortness of breath are all possible signs of PE.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + same-symptom purulent sputum outpatient clinic control (-cf).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic reference facts (31-year-old woman, 12-hour flight yesterday, birth control pill use, and coughing up blood today) with a 1-word span difference (8 vs 9 words) and 8 shared trailing tokens ('today so I need to go to the'). Swapping only f4 from coughing up blood to coughing up yellow phlegm changes sputum character within the same post-flight cough presentation while shifting care from emergency hospital PE evaluation (level 4) to outpatient clinic respiratory evaluation (level 2).
